subject: Locality proof, retention capability & retire-window — Q&A and proposed compromise
messages:
From: Elliott Marsh <elliott.marsh@atlashealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Legal <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on your retention/delete language + local proof ask

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for sending the DPA redline. Our legal team flagged two linked items we need clarity on before moving to internal approval:

1) "Retire window" / deletion timing: Section 4.2 refers to data being "retired within 60 days of request" but then notes backups may be retained for "a commercially reasonable period". Can you confirm the hard window for primary data deletion and the maximum backup snapshot retention you can commit to for Atlas Health? We need an upper bound.

2) Locality proof and evidence: we require demonstrable proof that Atlas data processed in the EU/US region is not exported outside the declared jurisdiction. The current wording points to "regionally scoped processing" but lacks operational evidence. Can you provide the types of artifacts Redwood can provide (audit logs, time-bound snapshots, certificate/scan reports) and their granularity?

I've attached our redline (Atlas_DPA_Redline_v3.docx).

Goal: get to a version we can send to procurement next week.

Best,
Elliott
Elliott Marsh
Head of Platform Security
Atlas Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elliott Marsh <elliott.marsh@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on your retention/delete language + local proof ask

Elliott — thanks for the clear summary and for the redline. Looping in Kimberly (security/compliance) and Marissa (legal) to propose an operational compromise. High level answers below, we can follow up with specific wording edits: 

• Primary deletion: Redwood can commit to removal of customer-accessible primary data (production replicas, object storage pointers, and model-extracted artifacts) within 30 calendar days of a validated erasure request.

• Backup snapshots: we keep periodic snapshots for disaster recovery. We can commit to a maximum backup retention of 90 calendar days for Atlas Health unless you require a shorter sec policy in the DPA; during that period backups will be marked for prioritized purge on a strict schedule and we will not use backups for any reprocessing of customer content.

• Locality proof: we can provide the following evidence artifacts on request —
  - Time-stamped region-assignment logs for ingestion and storage operations (CSV export)
  - Audit logs showing authoritative host-level residency for stored blobs
  - Snapshot manifest showing geo-zone and timestamp; optionally an attestation pdf for quarterly requests
  - Export / egress event reports if a cross-region fallback occurred (we can provide details for any such event)

Kimberly/Marissa — can you confirm whether the above commitments can be converted into DPA language (primary deletion = 30 days; backup TTL = 90 days; evidence types enumerated) and whether Atlas's redline needs narrower phrasing?

Next step: Marissa, legal can propose DPA text. Elliott, if those windows look broadly acceptable, we can prepare a short evidence playbook (redwood-locality-evidence-options.pdf) and a path to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product — Regions & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Elliott Marsh <elliott.marsh@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 13:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on your retention/delete language + local proof ask

Elliott — quick technical note to clarify what we can operationally guarantee and how we evidence it. I'm pasting the operational pieces so Marissa can translate to contract language.

1) What "delete primary data" means:
   - Delete of customer objects: when we accept an erasure request we remove object pointers and underlying blobs from active object stores and mark the keys for GC. At that time we also clear any model-level index entries and search caches that reference customer records.
   - KV/LLM caches: ephemeral KV caches (in-memory + local GPU caches) are flushed immediately; persistent caches are included in the primary delete flow.

2) Backups & snapshots:
   - Full snapshots are created nightly and retained for DR. They are stored in region-tagged buckets. We can commit to a non-negotiable maximum of 90 days retention for Atlas snapshots in the US region for this agreement.
   - After a deletion request, we will flag any snapshots containing Atlas data for expedited purge at the next snapshot lifecycle pass (within the 90-day window) and will provide a snapshot manifest indicating whether Atlas data was present and the purge status.

3) Evidence artifacts we can deliver (on request, delivery SLA):
   - Region assignment log (CSV): shows ingestion timestamp, assigned region, and storage bucket tag. SLA: delivered within 5 business days.
   - Snapshot manifest (PDF/CSV): list of snapshot IDs + region tag + retention expiry. SLA: 3 business days.
   - Audit log excerpt (JSON/CSV): actions against objects (create/delete/move) with timestamps. SLA: 5 business days.
   - Quarterly attestation: a signed PDF confirming region enforcement controls and any exceptions in the quarter. SLA: within 10 business days after quarter close.

4) Cross-region fallback: we do use a cross-region fallback policy for capacity failover. When a fallback occurs we will: 1) notify the customer by email within 24 hours; 2) provide an event report and 3) include the export event in the audit log export. We can also include a one-time review call for high-sensitivity customers.

Operational constraints / exceptions:
• Immutable third-party backups (rare): if Atlas requests an integration that uses a partner managed snapshot, the partner retention may be longer; we would call that out explicitly.
• Legal hold: any lawful hold communicated with appropriate paperwork will supersede deletion windows.

If this aligns with Atlas expectations, Marissa — please propose DPA clauses reflecting: 30-day primary delete, 90-day snapshot TTL, list of evidence items and SLAs, and an egress-notification commitment.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-locality-evidence-options.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliott Marsh <elliott.marsh@atlashealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Aug 2028 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on your retention/delete language + local proof ask

Elliott — thank you and Kim for the details. Draft contract language below for the two key items (we can refine):

Section 4.2 (Deletion of Customer Data) — Proposed text excerpt:
"Upon written request by Customer, Redwood will permanently delete Customer Data from its production systems within thirty (30) calendar days (the 'Primary Deletion Window'). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may retain backup snapshots for disaster recovery purposes for up to ninety (90) calendar days (the 'Backup Retention Period') following such deletion request. Redwood will flag and prioritize any backups containing Customer Data for purge at the next scheduled snapshot lifecycle pass and will not use such backups for model training, analytics, or reprocessing. Exception: lawful retention obligations or valid legal holds submitted by Customer or a competent authority will supersede the Primary Deletion Window and Backup Retention Period so long as such obligations remain in effect."

Section X (Residency Evidence & Reporting) — Proposed text excerpt:
"Upon request, Redwood will provide the Customer with the following evidence artifacts describing the geographic processing and storage of Customer Data: (a) region-assignment logs; (b) snapshot manifests indicating region tags and retention expiries; (c) audit log excerpts evidencing object lifecycle events; and (d) a quarterly attestation of regional controls. Redwood will deliver such artifacts within the SLAs specified in the applicable evidence playbook. Redwood will notify Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of any cross-region fallback or emergency export event and will provide a report describing scope and duration within three (3) business days."

If Atlas is comfortable with this compromise, we can incorporate into a tracked DPA and route for signature. Jonas — please confirm if you want any additional operational limits (e.g., stricter snapshot TTL for certain buckets) and Kim — confirm SLAs above.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elliott Marsh <elliott.marsh@atlashealth.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on your retention/delete language + local proof ask

Marissa / Kim / Jonas — appreciate the fast turnaround. Atlas Legal reviewed the proposed text and the evidence SLAs. Two quick asks before we finalize: 

1) Can you make the backup purge manifest auditable (hash/signature) so we can verify a purge occurred for a flagged snapshot? A simple signed manifest PDF would be acceptable.
2) For the 24-hour cross-region notification, can you add a one-business-day maximum for the initial notice to be sent to our security contact (we need to ensure we receive it within business hours)?

If you confirm those two points, we’ll accept the compromise and move to DocuSign.

Elliott
Elliott Marsh
Head of Platform Security
Atlas Health
